name: ux-oss-safeguard
entry: - [ux-oss-safeguard](https://github.com/actually-useful-ai/ux-oss-safeguard) - Content safety evaluator with WCAG 2.1 AA support, keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, and reduced-motion handling. Zero dependencies.

name: All-in-One Accessibility
entry: - [All-in-One Accessibility](https://www.skynettechnologies.com/all-in-one-accessibility) - Widget for Django, Wagtail and Plone that wraps a commercial service. Open source (MIT).

name: Dock Access
entry: - [Dock Access](https://dockaccess.org/) - Commercial accessibility suite with a user-facing widget, automated audits, monitoring and manual audits. (Free browser extension and paid services)

name: UserWay
entry: - [UserWay](https://userway.org/) - Commercial accessibility overlay widget.

name: WCAG Watch
entry: - [WCAG Watch](https://wcagwatch.tirelesslabs.com) - Automated technical WCAG/EAA monitoring for EU-facing sites, built on axe-core. Free instant scan; paid continuous monitoring from €29/mo. Note: automated scanners catch only an estimated 25–33% of WCAG issues — not a substitute for a human audit or legal/compliance certification.

name: axe MCP Server
entry: - [axe MCP Server](https://www.deque.com/axe/mcp-server/) - Deque's MCP server that lets AI coding agents run axe scans and get remediation guidance in the editor. Commercial; requires an axe DevTools subscription.

name: Duxbury Braille Translator
entry: - [Duxbury Braille Translator](https://www.duxburysystems.com/) - Commercial braille translation and formatting software widely used by transcribers and schools.

name: BlindSquare
entry: - [BlindSquare](https://www.blindsquare.com/) - Paid iOS GPS app for blind and deafblind travelers that describes surroundings and announces intersections and points of interest.

name: Glide
entry: - [Glide](https://www.glidance.io/) - Wheeled mobility aid for blind and low-vision people that uses cameras and AI to steer around obstacles; rolling out in the U.S., Canada and the UK in 2026, with a monthly subscription.

name: WeWALK Smart Cane 2
entry: - [WeWALK Smart Cane 2](https://wewalk.io/) - Smart handle for a white cane with obstacle detection, voice-guided navigation and an AI voice assistant.

name: Dragon Professional
entry: - [Dragon Professional](https://dragon.nuance.com/) - Commercial speech recognition for Windows with dictation and voice control of applications, long a standard for people who cannot use a keyboard.

name: ModelTalker
entry: - [ModelTalker](https://www.modeltalker.org/) - Voice banking service from the Nemours Speech Research Lab that builds a personal synthetic voice for people expecting to lose their speech.

name: SpeakUnique
entry: - [SpeakUnique](https://www.speakunique.co.uk/) - UK voice banking and voice repair service that can build a personal synthetic voice even from recordings of already-affected speech.

name: An Introduction to Accessibility and Inclusive Design
entry: - [An Introduction to Accessibility and Inclusive Design](https://www.coursera.org/learn/accessibility) - University of Illinois course on Coursera covering disability, assistive technology, law and universal design. Free to audit.

name: Accessible UX Research
entry: - [Accessible UX Research](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/printed-books/accessible-ux-research/) - Michele A. Williams (Smashing Media, 2026). Practical guide to planning, recruiting for and running UX research with disabled participants.

name: Being Heumann
entry: - [Being Heumann](https://www.beacon.org/Being-Heumann-P1618.aspx) - Judith Heumann with Kristen Joiner (Beacon Press, 2020). Memoir of a disability rights leader, including the 1977 Section 504 sit-in.

name: Disability Visibility
entry: - [Disability Visibility](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/617802/disability-visibility-by-alice-wong/) - Alice Wong, editor (Vintage, 2020). Anthology of first-person essays by disabled writers on disability culture and lived experience.

name: Form Design Patterns
entry: - [Form Design Patterns](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/printed-books/form-design-patterns/) - Adam Silver (Smashing Media, 2018). Works through real forms and builds a set of accessible form components along the way.

name: Inclusive Components: The Book
entry: - [Inclusive Components: The Book](https://book.inclusive-components.design/) - Heydon Pickering (2019). Expanded edition of the Inclusive Components blog on building common interface patterns accessibly.

name: Inclusive Design for a Digital World
entry: - [Inclusive Design for a Digital World](https://link.springer.com/book/9798868818196) - Regine Gilbert (Apress, 2025). Second edition of an introduction to accessible product design, covering WCAG 2.2, the European Accessibility Act and AI.

name: Mismatch
entry: - [Mismatch](https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262539487/mismatch/) - Kat Holmes (MIT Press, 2018). How design choices exclude people, and the case for designing with excluded communities.

name: Practical Web Accessibility
entry: - [Practical Web Accessibility](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/979-8-8688-0152-5) - Ashley Firth (Apress, 2024). Second edition of a guide organized around access needs, updated for WCAG 2.2.

name: Web Accessibility Cookbook
entry: - [Web Accessibility Cookbook](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/web-accessibility-cookbook/9781098145590/) - Manuel Matuzović (O'Reilly, 2024). Recipes for building common components accessibly, including navigation, dialogs, filters and data tables.

name: A Web for Everyone
entry: - [A Web for Everyone](https://rosenfeldmedia.com/books/a-web-for-everyone/) - Sarah Horton and Whitney Quesenbery (Rosenfeld Media, 2014). UX-centered guide to accessible design built on universal design principles.
